The original `scale_capacity_v1` population fixes the main dirty budget at 200. Earlier 100k runs reached the registered five-hour limit before completing every mutation checkpoint. Their failures, budgets, source identities and raw records remain unchanged. This PR registers a separate configuration for measuring the complete incremental workload with a larger dirty budget.

## What changes

Register `scale_wide_dirty_v1` with main dirty budget 4096 and resume limit 1024. Preserve the original 200/1024 profile and product defaults, the continuous mutation history, all no-op/body/API/config/batch stages, full-control builds and all 15 parity tables. The independent fanout population continues to use 8/128 and must actually demonstrate incomplete work followed by closure.

Both configurations retain the same physical streaming oracle contract. Results keep separate profile, source, binary, seed and shard identities; aggregation rejects mixed or missing populations. The independent workflow retains the original five scales, 30 repetitions per scale, 150 shards / 1500 samples, seed 12648430, and measurement capacity/time boundaries. It uses label `p8-scale-wide-dirty-run` and separate artifact names.

Also apply the nine formatting changes reported by the original PR193 check to four inherited source/test files. The failed check and running G8 study remain attached to their original source.

## Validation and current boundary

The original 39 Python protocol tests are unchanged. All 44 tests, including five new profile/aggregate controls, passed on these exact driver/test bytes. Independent source review verifies the actual product and validation inventories and preserves all earlier reviews. These are source and protocol results; native execution and scale performance remain pending.

Before a fresh release producer is built, the new workflow runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the original `cc-eval` `p8_scale` integration target in a separate target directory. This PR remains a draft while its actual engineering checks and measurements are reviewed.

No original TODO is marked complete by this PR. A complete population can support its declared 4096 configuration; it cannot repair or replace the registered 200 population, establish a causal speedup, or justify a stable p99 claim.

## Source and study identities

This PR uses frozen base `base/p8-G8-wide-bfcc-20261009` at `4fe927488d5cb7f26bd27c7624745fb1b6ca202b`, the original G8 source from PR193. This keeps the new study independently testable while PR193 receives its own engineering fixes. Final integration with main will use the actual accepted source and resolve its source bindings explicitly. Exact product/review/guard commits and the actual new run are recorded below after publication.

The original `scale_capacity_v1` population fixes the main dirty budget at 200. Earlier 100k runs reached the registered five-hour limit before completing every mutation checkpoint. Their failures, budgets, source identities and raw records remain unchanged. This PR registers a separate configuration for measuring the complete incremental workload with a larger dirty budget.

## What changes

Register `scale_wide_dirty_v1` with main dirty budget 4096 and resume limit 1024. Preserve the original 200/1024 profile and product defaults, the continuous mutation history, all no-op/body/API/config/batch stages, full-control builds and all 15 parity tables. The independent fanout population continues to use 8/128 and must actually demonstrate incomplete work followed by closure.

Both configurations retain the same physical streaming oracle contract. Results keep separate profile, source, binary, seed and shard identities; aggregation rejects mixed or missing populations. The independent workflow retains the original five scales, 30 repetitions per scale, 150 shards / 1500 samples, seed 12648430, and measurement capacity/time boundaries. It uses label `p8-scale-wide-dirty-run` and separate artifact names.

Also apply the nine formatting changes reported by the original PR193 check to four inherited source/test files. The failed check and running G8 study remain attached to their original source.

## Validation and current boundary

The original 39 Python protocol tests are unchanged. All 44 tests, including five new profile/aggregate controls, passed on these exact driver/test bytes. Independent source review verifies the actual product and validation inventories and preserves all earlier reviews. These are source and protocol results; native execution and scale performance remain pending.

Before a fresh release producer is built, the new workflow runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the original `cc-eval` `p8_scale` integration target in a separate target directory. This PR remains a draft while its actual engineering checks and measurements are reviewed.

No original TODO is marked complete by this PR. A complete population can support its declared 4096 configuration; it cannot repair or replace the registered 200 population, establish a causal speedup, or justify a stable p99 claim.

## Source and study identities

This PR uses frozen base `base/p8-G8-wide-bfcc-20261009` at `4fe927488d5cb7f26bd27c7624745fb1b6ca202b`, the original G8 source from PR193. This keeps the new study independently testable while PR193 receives its own engineering fixes. Final integration with main will use the actual accepted source and resolve its source bindings explicitly. Exact product/review/guard commits and the actual new run are recorded below after publication.

- Product: `04e77a0f401419aa2192051b3992498a56c4ea01` (tree `ff5315a01fca3d2e003df999503069920ae44d6a`).

issue.title: test(eval): register an independent wide dirty scale configuration
issue.body:
## Why this change is needed

The original `scale_capacity_v1` population fixes the main dirty budget at 200. Earlier 100k runs reached the registered five-hour limit before completing every mutation checkpoint. Their failures, budgets, source identities and raw records remain unchanged. This PR registers a separate configuration for measuring the complete incremental workload with a larger dirty budget.

## What changes

Register `scale_wide_dirty_v1` with main dirty budget 4096 and resume limit 1024. Preserve the original 200/1024 profile and product defaults, the continuous mutation history, all no-op/body/API/config/batch stages, full-control builds and all 15 parity tables. The independent fanout population continues to use 8/128 and must actually demonstrate incomplete work followed by closure.

Both configurations retain the same physical streaming oracle contract. Results keep separate profile, source, binary, seed and shard identities; aggregation rejects mixed or missing populations. The independent workflow retains the original five scales, 30 repetitions per scale, 150 shards / 1500 samples, seed 12648430, and measurement capacity/time boundaries. It uses label `p8-scale-wide-dirty-run` and separate artifact names.

Also apply the nine formatting changes reported by the original PR193 check to four inherited source/test files. The failed check and running G8 study remain attached to their original source.

## Validation and current boundary

The original 39 Python protocol tests are unchanged. All 44 tests, including five new profile/aggregate controls, passed on these exact driver/test bytes. Independent source review verifies the actual product and validation inventories and preserves all earlier reviews. These are source and protocol results; native execution and scale performance remain pending.

Before a fresh release producer is built, the new workflow runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the original `cc-eval` `p8_scale` integration target in a separate target directory. This PR remains a draft while its actual engineering checks and measurements are reviewed.

No original TODO is marked complete by this PR. A complete population can support its declared 4096 configuration; it cannot repair or replace the registered 200 population, establish a causal speedup, or justify a stable p99 claim.

## Source and study identities

This PR uses frozen base `base/p8-G8-wide-bfcc-20261009` at `4fe927488d5cb7f26bd27c7624745fb1b6ca202b`, the original G8 source from PR193. This keeps the new study independently testable while PR193 receives its own engineering fixes. Final integration with main will use the actual accepted source and resolve its source bindings explicitly. Exact product/review/guard commits and the actual new run are recorded below after publication.

- Product: `04e77a0f401419aa2192051b3992498a56c4ea01` (tree `ff5315a01fca3d2e003df999503069920ae44d6a`).
- Independent source review: `4b1c0a7f0b682a5e0d34d9fab6eb1e8955f03386`, adding only the canonical review and original source proof.
- Bound study source: `a9448ecadd713b061823ecb96578791f800c0ae7` (tree `1dd376d2d6311ed0ecebafcbb562bbfe03783c0c`), adding only the two current source-binding files.
- Product inventory: 1095 files; 75 differences against the original BASE; 143 validation inputs.
- The original source-only review at `8ef97e53c5ce5d9fb6d89346b1d94ef946710fe1` and all earlier reviews remain in history.
- The original G8/200 run remains [37962416564, attempt 1](https://github.com/jyqj/codecortex/actions/runs/37962416564), source `4fe927488d5cb7f26bd27c7624745fb1b6ca202b`. It is independent of the forthcoming wide run.

GW3 原启动结果和本次最小修复：

[Run37976092549 / build113974644200](https://github.com/jyqj/codecortex/actions/runs/37976092549/job/113974644200) 的 rustfmt 已实际执行，并发现一处新数组布局不符，以及稀疏 checkout 缺少现有测试引用的 artifact Rust 源码。该原运行保持 failure；原 Rust 协议测试、release producer 与测量均未开始，测量信用为0。

本次仅按实际 formatter hunk展开两元素数组，并在 build checkout补入两份确实被引用的源文件：`current-status-under-test.rs` 和 `v2-status-checks.rs`。有界源审确认它们没有继续向外引用其他文件，原 sparse-pattern控制实际通过。原 formatter/test命令、N、预算、profile、fanout和物理oracle约束均保持不变。

实际源链：
- P `0fa6d35256a59f51a8be2ecc9c49ee85d842aa6c`
- 独立R `a61ab54a7cbad41db3e17fb4b4d628ec217de5a8`
- 当前G `008f1ec0ae16b9b6aff9f20d033b17b2219168f8`
- tree `d5ce466ab3ccde1f00dad693e39ebfa07f051f3b`

绑定生成器此次已实际以Python退出0；独立检查确认恰6个registry字段、4个literal pins及原完整输入映射。该结果仍仅为源码准入准备，不能替代新的Rust/CI实测。接下来以新G启动一个独立运行，保留两次旧启动失败和各自源码身份。原G8/cold研究不变，TODO仍163/192完成、29剩余。

The original `scale_capacity_v1` population fixes the main dirty budget at 200. Earlier 100k runs reached the registered five-hour limit before completing every mutation checkpoint. Their failures, budgets, source identities and raw records remain unchanged. This PR registers a separate configuration for measuring the complete incremental workload with a larger dirty budget.

## What changes

Register `scale_wide_dirty_v1` with main dirty budget 4096 and resume limit 1024. Preserve the original 200/1024 profile and product defaults, the continuous mutation history, all no-op/body/API/config/batch stages, full-control builds and all 15 parity tables. The independent fanout population continues to use 8/128 and must actually demonstrate incomplete work followed by closure.

Both configurations retain the same physical streaming oracle contract. Results keep separate profile, source, binary, seed and shard identities; aggregation rejects mixed or missing populations. The independent workflow retains the original five scales, 30 repetitions per scale, 150 shards / 1500 samples, seed 12648430, and measurement capacity/time boundaries. It uses label `p8-scale-wide-dirty-run` and separate artifact names.

Also apply the nine formatting changes reported by the original PR193 check to four inherited source/test files. The failed check and running G8 study remain attached to their original source.

## Validation and current boundary

The original 39 Python protocol tests are unchanged. All 44 tests, including five new profile/aggregate controls, passed on these exact driver/test bytes. Independent source review verifies the actual product and validation inventories and preserves all earlier reviews. These are source and protocol results; native execution and scale performance remain pending.

Before a fresh release producer is built, the new workflow runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the original `cc-eval` `p8_scale` integration target in a separate target directory. This PR remains a draft while its actual engineering checks and measurements are reviewed.

No original TODO is marked complete by this PR. A complete population can support its declared 4096 configuration; it cannot repair or replace the registered 200 population, establish a causal speedup, or justify a stable p99 claim.

## Source and study identities

This PR uses frozen base `base/p8-G8-wide-bfcc-20261009` at `4fe927488d5cb7f26bd27c7624745fb1b6ca202b`, the original G8 source from PR193. This keeps the new study independently testable while PR193 receives its own engineering fixes. Final integration with main will use the actual accepted source and resolve its source bindings explicitly. ## Why this change is needed

The cold-build and continuous dirty-scale studies currently live on separate reviewed branches. Their shared driver and Rust protocol code need one source that preserves both contracts and can pass the unchanged normal CI before integration into `main`.

This PR integrates the reviewed payload/cell-witness source from #193, the cold protocol from #189, and the explicit wide dirty-plan protocol from #194. The initial merge preserves the non-overlapping donor edits and existing review artifacts. Follow-up repairs address the exact Rust formatter hunk and the two existing Rust modules omitted by the wide build's sparse checkout.

## Resulting behavior

- Cold samples retain two fresh A/B full builds and all fifteen canonical-table comparisons. The original cold study remains bound to source `044c008c9459cfa61e7701db2eb868342c508a39`, run `37954851017`, attempt 1.
- The explicit `scale_wide_dirty_v1` profile uses a 4096/1024 main work plan. The existing `scale_capacity_v1` plan remains 200/1024, and product defaults remain unchanged. Both preserve the separate 8/128 fanout plan, incomplete-build closure, full controls and parity checks.
- The wide workflow installs the required rustfmt component and includes the two actual external Rust test modules in its build checkout. Its registered five scales × N30 population, worker deadline, output limit and concurrency remain unchanged.
- Existing failure records, old source identities, validators and TODO dependencies remain intact. No original TODO is marked complete here.

## Review and verification

The source commit is `58a890857a6b6c2da874491817beb6d561897a9a`. Independent review commit `b39fdd8c858755d1a92c176efc5340907f4a3757` covers 1095 product inputs, 75 BASE differences and 146 validation inputs. Its canonical report is `artifacts/checkpoints/p8-cold-wide-startup-integration-bfcc-20261009/independent-source-review.json`.

This PR head `34dc4e14dc96d077eae6173ab6885370323eff3f` has that review as its sole parent and changes exactly the two source-binding files. The six registry fields and four guard pins were independently checked against the actual source/review and the computed tree.

The original 44 scale-driver and 12 cold-driver Python controls actually passed on the five-file PCW2 projection (`da6289df86dd228e810a63b90f4be03c34b8d21b`), with no skipped tests and unchanged inputs before/after. Those five files are byte-identical in the final source; their execution identity is retained. This is not a claim that the final source's native Rust tests or whole CI have already passed.

An additional CI step was proposed and rejected because the original v15 verifier requires the original CI file. The final source restores that file exactly; neither the verifier nor any test threshold was relaxed.

## Open acceptance work

This remains Draft while the final source's actual normal CI and source guards run. The earlier #193 check failed the original warm-index fixture at 556.28 ms against the unchanged 500 ms limit; its failure remains recorded. Both earlier wide startup failures also remain recorded and contributed zero measurements. The repaired wide study is separately bound to `008f1ec0ae16b9b6aff9f20d033b17b2219168f8`, run `37982220020`, attempt 1.

The original G8 full study has accepted 4/150 shards and 41/1500 samples; the cold study's last declared intake is 16/150, of which 10 have published original custody. New successful Actions jobs are still subject to original intake. Populations are not pooled and this PR makes no completed-scale or speed claim.

Original task ledger: **192 total / 163 done / 29 remaining / 0 newly completed**. At least ten original tasks will be closed only when their existing acceptance criteria and dependency chain are fulfilled.

The cold-build and continuous dirty-scale studies currently live on separate reviewed branches. Their shared driver and Rust protocol code need one source that preserves both contracts and can pass the unchanged normal CI before integration into `main`.

This PR integrates the reviewed payload/cell-witness source from #193, the cold protocol from #189, and the explicit wide dirty-plan protocol from #194. The initial merge preserves the non-overlapping donor edits and existing review artifacts. Follow-up repairs address the exact Rust formatter hunk and the two existing Rust modules omitted by the wide build's sparse checkout.

## Resulting behavior

- Cold samples retain two fresh A/B full builds and all fifteen canonical-table comparisons. The original cold study remains bound to source `044c008c9459cfa61e7701db2eb868342c508a39`, run `37954851017`, attempt 1.
- The explicit `scale_wide_dirty_v1` profile uses a 4096/1024 main work plan. The existing `scale_capacity_v1` plan remains 200/1024, and product defaults remain unchanged. Both preserve the separate 8/128 fanout plan, incomplete-build closure, full controls and parity checks.
- The wide workflow installs the required rustfmt component and includes the two actual external Rust test modules in its build checkout. Its registered five scales × N30 population, worker deadline, output limit and concurrency remain unchanged.
- Existing failure records, old source identities, validators and TODO dependencies remain intact. No original TODO is marked complete here.

## Review and verification

The source commit is `58a890857a6b6c2da874491817beb6d561897a9a`. Independent review commit `b39fdd8c858755d1a92c176efc5340907f4a3757` covers 1095 product inputs, 75 BASE differences and 146 validation inputs. Its canonical report is `artifacts/checkpoints/p8-cold-wide-startup-integration-bfcc-20261009/independent-source-review.json`.

This PR head `34dc4e14dc96d077eae6173ab6885370323eff3f` has that review as its sole parent and changes exactly the two source-binding files. The six registry fields and four guard pins were independently checked against the actual source/review and the computed tree.

The original 44 scale-driver and 12 cold-driver Python controls actually passed on the five-file PCW2 projection (`da6289df86dd228e810a63b90f4be03c34b8d21b`), with no skipped tests and unchanged inputs before/after. Those five files are byte-identical in the final source; their execution identity is retained. This is not a claim that the final source's native Rust tests or whole CI have already passed.

An additional CI step was proposed and rejected because the original v15 verifier requires the original CI file. The final source restores that file exactly; neither the verifier nor any test threshold was relaxed.

## Open acceptance work

This remains Draft while the final source's actual normal CI and source guards run. The earlier #193 check failed the original warm-index fixture at 556.28 ms against the unchanged 500 ms limit; its failure remains recorded. Both earlier wide startup failures also remain recorded and contributed zero measurements. The repaired wide study is separately bound to `008f1ec0ae16b9b6aff9f20d033b17b2219168f8`, run `37982220020`, attempt 1.

The original G8 full study has accepted 4/150 shards and 41/1500 samples; the cold study's last declared intake is 16/150, of which 10 have published original custody. New successful Actions jobs are still subject to original intake. Populations are not pooled and this PR makes no completed-scale or speed claim.
